true_answer: Proofs might seem scary (especially if you have had a bad high school geometry experience) but all we are really doing is explaining (very carefully) why a statement is true. If you understand the truth conditions for an implication, you already have the outline for a proof. Direct Proofs of Implications. To prove an implication P → Q , it is enough to assume P , and from it, deduce Q . Perhaps a better way to say this is that to prove a statement of the form P → Q directly, you must explain why Q is true, but you get to assume P is true first.
